name: Relapsing Polychondritis

diagnosticCriteria.formalCriteriaName: McAdam Criteria (Modified by Damiani and Levine)

criteria.description: Ocular inflammation (conjunctivitis, keratitis, scleritis, episcleritis, uveitis)
Respiratory tract chondritis (laryngeal and/or tracheal cartilages)
Cochlear and/or vestibular dysfunction (neurosensory hearing loss, tinnitus, vertigo)
Histological confirmation of chondritis in biopsy specimen

diagnosticCriteria.minimumForDiagnosis: McAdam: 3 or more of the 6 clinical features. Damiani modification: 1 clinical feature + histological confirmation, OR 2 clinical features responding to steroids. Biopsy not always required.
diagnosticCriteria.notes: 30% of patients have another autoimmune condition (vasculitis, RA, SLE, MDS). MAGIC syndrome: RP + Behcet disease. VEXAS syndrome should be excluded in males with MDS features.

pathognomonic.symptomName: Auricular chondritis (red, swollen, painful ear pinna sparing lobe)
pathognomonic.notes: Most common presenting feature; ear lobe spared (no cartilage). Eventually causes floppy/cauliflower ear.

common.symptomName: Nasal chondritis with saddle nose deformity
common.notes: Nasal bridge pain and swelling; progressive collapse leads to saddle nose
Can be life-threatening; tracheal collapse or subglottic stenosis

rare.notes: From destruction of aortic root cartilage/connective tissue

laboratory: Elevated ESR and CRP during flares
Anti-type II collagen antibodies (present in ~30-50%; not routinely available)
imaging: CT airway: tracheal/bronchial wall thickening, narrowing, calcification
Dynamic CT or MRI: tracheobronchomalacia on expiratory imaging
PET-CT: FDG uptake in inflamed cartilage
Echocardiography: aortic root dilation, valve regurgitation
genetic: UBA1 gene mutation testing to exclude VEXAS syndrome (somatic mutation in males)
other: Pulmonary function tests: fixed upper airway obstruction pattern, flow-volume loop flattening
Cartilage biopsy: loss of basophilic staining, perichondrial inflammation, chondrocyte depletion
Bronchoscopy: airway inflammation, collapse, stenosis (but carries airway compromise risk)

distinguishingFeatures: GPA has saddle nose but also sinus/lung/kidney involvement
RA has erosive arthritis, positive RF/anti-CCP
RA does not affect cartilage of ear/nose
IgA vasculitis (HSP) has palpable purpura, nephritis, GI symptoms
IgA vasculitis biopsy shows IgA deposits

redFlags: Stridor or progressive dyspnea (life-threatening airway compromise)
New cardiac murmur (aortic regurgitation from aortitis)
Features of VEXAS syndrome (MDS, thrombosis, macrocytosis in males)
references: McAdam LP, et al. Relapsing polychondritis: prospective study of 23 patients and a review of the literature. Medicine (Baltimore). 1976;55(3):193-215.
Borgia F, et al. Relapsing polychondritis: an updated review. Biomedicines. 2018;6(3):84.
Kingdon J, et al. Relapsing polychondritis: a clinical review for rheumatologists. Rheumatology (Oxford). 2018;57(9):1525-1532.
